sbic_candidates.name: Social Bias Inference Corpus (SBIC)
sbic_candidates.source_paper: Can Large Language Models Transform Computational Social Science?
findings: The paper defines Social Bias Inference Corpus (SBIC) as a task involving free-text explanations of the implicit social meaning of hateful or biased statements.
Section 3.4.3 states the corpus contains approximately 34,000 inferences and cites Sap et al. (2020).
Table 4 reports ChatGPT at 65.9% in the SBIC column for expert human evaluations of zero-shot generation.
sbic_candidates.metric_interpretation: 65.9% is the share of pairwise expert rankings in which the authors unanimously preferred a model-generated explanation as more accurate or preferable to the human gold explanation. It is not 65.9% classification accuracy, forecast accuracy, or a financial prediction metric.
sbic_candidates.relevance: A plausible referent for the exact phrase 'ChatGPT SBIC'; unrelated to the Japanese investment company and unrelated to XRP.

sbic_candidates.note: A Chinese-language PDF search extraction describes an SBIC label as social and behavioral impacts of COVID-19 and shows a ChatGPT preference table. The original dataset title and acronym expansion have not been verified against the paper's source-language text. Do not merge this candidate with Social Bias Inference Corpus.
